pageCache.pageTitle: About Releasing Potential – Releasing Potential School
pageCache.text:
Releasing Potential's Journey
Founded in 2001 by Mike King, Releasing Potential helps marginalised young people develop essential life skills through innovative outdoor education. What began with sessions run from a Portsmouth home has evolved into a comprehensive educational organisation, serving vulnerable students across Hampshire and West Sussex.
By 2011, responding to increasing referrals from Local Authorities, Mike established the first full-time programme in Havant – the Engage programme. The success with young people who struggled in conventional school environments led to the registration of an Independent School in 2017 and an Alternative Provision in 2024, both of which cater for children with an Education Health Care Plan.
Our Evolution
From these humble beginnings, Releasing Potential has grown into a comprehensive educational organisation. Our success with young people led to the establishment of an Independent School, which offers a range of opportunities from the indoors to the outdoor learning environment.
Our journey reflects our commitment to responding to community needs while maintaining the core values that have always driven our work: unconditional positive regard, outdoor learning, and personalised support.
We believe that every young person has innate capabilities waiting to be discovered. By creating environments where they feel safe yet challenged we nurture their abilities to take risks – leading to breakthroughs in social and emotional development.
Multiple Sites across Hampshire and West Sussex
Our Team
The Releasing Potential team comprises a diverse group of experienced educators and specialists committed to transforming young lives:
Each member brings a wealth of knowledge and experience from various educational backgrounds, ensuring our approach balances academic excellence and personal development.
Therapeutic Practitioners supporting emotional and social development
Academic Staff delivering engaging curriculum content
Our Impact
Since 2001, Releasing Potential has:
By combining educational excellence with therapeutic support and real-world experiences, we help young people not only overcome barriers to learning but discover strengths they never knew they possessed.
Developed comprehensive pathways from intervention to independence
Created employment opportunities through our social enterprises
Our Governance
Releasing Potential operates with transparent governance and oversight:
Our Board of Trustees brings together professionals from education, business, and community sectors, providing strategic guidance and ensuring we remain true to our founding mission while adapting to meet evolving needs.
Want to refer a young person to our services? We welcome enquiries from education professionals, parents, carers and local authorities about 11-18 years olds who might benefit from our personalised approach to learning and development.

pageCache.pageTitle: Special Educational Needs – Releasing Potential School
pageCache.text:
Specialising in working with children with Special Educational Needs (S.E.N)
Tailored Support
We have developed strategies, over many years of experience in this sector, to support students in managing their responses to stress and anxiety; in turn they are able to make progress in academic and social areas. We specialise in working with challenging behaviour and are able to tailor programmes of learning and support to suit individual needs and concerns. As part of our commitment to breaking down barriers to inclusion, we do not require students to wear a school uniform.
By the end of Year 11 students have a college place, or other appropriate next destination; they have qualifications up to Level 1 in a range of academic and vocational subjects, and the social and emotional skills to cope with whatever comes next.
*Please note: an SEN Information Report is not available as a separate document, as all students have registered SEND. Admission arrangements can be found in our Accessibility Plan and Admissions Policy.

About Releasing Potential
Find out more about our story and what we do.
Find out more about us >
Governed with integrity
Our Board of Trustees, chaired by Paul Jenkins, provides strategic oversight and ensures our unwavering commitment to our founding principles. The full Board meets quarterly to review progress, maintain accountability, and ensure every aspect of our work advances our charitable mission.
Financial resilience through a multifaceted approach
As a charity, we’ve developed a multifaceted approach to financial resilience and long-term viability.
This integrated model allows us to maintain our commitment to vulnerable young people regardless of economic pressures, whilst creating meaningful pathways for students to develop workplace skills in supportive environments.
Support our vision
As a registered charity, we welcome support from individuals, businesses and trusts who share our belief in the transformative power of unconditional positive regard. Whether through financial contributions, partnerships, or volunteering, every form of support directly enhances our capacity to create environments where young people discover capabilities they never knew they possessed.
The young people we work with have often experienced significant disruption in their educational journeys. Your support helps ensure we can provide the consistent, compassionate presence they need to rebuild trust and reclaim their potential. Contact us if you’d like to get involved.

pageCache.pageTitle: Join our team – Releasing Potential School
pageCache.text:
Thinking about joining Releasing Potential?
You're in the right place!
Every great career starts with curiosity and a few questions. Whether you’re an experienced in SEN or exploring this path for the first time, we want you to feel informed and inspired.
Below, we’ve answered some of the most common questions from candidates just like you – people who are passionate about making a real difference and wondering if RP is the right fit.
From our values (Choice Theory is a big part of them)
To how we support our staff (yes, including a generous pension and actual salary), you’ll find everything you need to take the next step with confidence.
Work Structure & Locations
How many hours will I work each day? You’ll work a standard 8-hour day.
Can I work part-time? Yes, part-time roles are available. These typically involve working fewer full days per week, not shorter daily hours. This ensures consistency and structure for our pupils.
Pupil Support & Approach
What is the pupil-to-staff ratio? We maintain high staffing levels to meet individual needs. Staff typically support pupils on a 1:1 basis or in very small groups, allowing for tailored support and strong relationships.
Pay, Benefits & Development
Is the salary pro-rated for school holidays? No. Salaries are actual, not pro-rated, meaning you are paid your full contracted salary regardless of holiday periods.
Is there a pension scheme? Yes. We offer a generous pension scheme, providing valuable long-term financial benefits for our staff.
Is there a career path? Absolutely. We actively support your professional growth through CPD, training, and opportunities for progression.
Culture, Values & Wellbeing
What is the organisation’s approach to behaviour and relationships? Our values are guided by Glasser’s Choice Theory and a strong belief in positive reinforcement. We focus on building meaningful relationships, encouraging internal motivation, and fostering a sense of belonging and responsibility.
What is the company culture like? Inclusive, supportive, and learner centred. We work as a team and share a passion for making a meaningful difference in the lives of young people with SEN. Staff are valued, heard, and encouraged to grow.
Is there a good work/life balance? Yes. We understand the demands of SEN education and actively promote a healthy balance through clear structures, manageable expectations and strong leadership support.
Further questions and what you can do now
Have more questions? We’d love to hear from you. Get in touch with Jill at jill@releasingpotential.com or call 07563 024063

pageCache.pageTitle: Meet the team – Releasing Potential School
pageCache.text:
Our leadership team
Executive Board
Mike King
Mike founded Releasing Potential in 2001, driven by his passion for creating bridges between marginalised young people and wider society. With a B.Ed and background as a PE teacher, he brings extensive outdoor education qualifications to his leadership role. As CEO, Mike oversees strategic direction while still finding time to teach outdoor education sessions.
Mike has a particular enthusiasm for sailing along the South Coast and hiking in the mountains.
Jane Skinner
Jane has been with Releasing Potential since its inception in 2001, providing crucial financial stewardship throughout the organisation’s growth and development. With over 30 years’ experience in finance and senior management positions, she brings invaluable expertise to her role. As CFO, Jane ensures strong administrative foundations that empower our educational teams.
Jane has a particular enjoyment for walking, reading and kayaking.
Olly Parker
Olly joined Releasing Potential in 2024, bringing over 25 years of experience in education and leadership to his role. With an MA in Education and extensive background in supporting learners with additional needs, he specialises in creating environments where young people with SEMH needs can thrive. As Head of School, Olly ensures our provision delivers meaningful progression pathways.
Olly has a particular interest in automotive and motorsport events, especially vintage tractor shows.
Emma Jones
Emma joined Releasing Potential in 2018, bringing valuable experience from her career in the outdoor industry. With a degree in outdoor education and specialist knowledge in water sports, she has transformed our approach to experiential learning. As our Outdoor Education Manager Emma enhances both the quality and capacity of our facilities.
Emma has a particular passion for windsurfing and paddle boarding, often enjoying water sports with her son and dog along the coast.
Deputy heads
Lesley Brown
Lesley joined Releasing Potential in 2019 after having previously worked in primary provision and works as a Mentor 1:1 with students. She specialises in using her creative talents to support students in practical activities and runs our RP Printing business, offering work placements to Year 11 and post-16 students.
Carol Page
Carol is a qualified teacher and joined Releasing Potential in March 2021 as Functional Skills Lead; she has been Curriculum Lead since May 2022. Carol has a wealth of experience in teaching Functional Skills in FE colleges and for private training providers. She is responsible for overseeing the delivery of the curriculum within RP School. Carol is married with 2 children and enjoys travelling, spending time with her family and walking her two dogs.
Russell Tapley
Russell has returned to RP after a 7-year hiatus during which he has worked with a range of Youth Work organisations as a senior manager. He leads on behaviour, family liaison and transition – providing bespoke 1:1 sessions aimed at enabling students who have been out of education to transition to the RP School and access the full curriculum.
Outdoor Education
Sarah West
Sarah has worked in education and the community for 22 years and has developed a passion for working with children with SEMH difficulties. She has a BA (Hons) in Childhood Studies and brings her enthusiasm for the outdoors to her work with students, having joined Releasing Potential in 2019 as a mentor working 1:1 with young people.
Nick Peacock
Nick joined Releasing Potential in October 2021 having previously worked as a teacher in an Independent SEN SEMH school and has a degree in Adventure Education and a PGCE in Primary Education. His background in the outdoors comes from the world of Paddlesport where he has worked with a variety of centres and clubs, helping to overhaul procedures whilst leading on British Canoeing and IOL inspections.
